text:
maya: Hey team — incoming customer escalation. Customer sees intermittent 429 spikes for org_id=acme-inc, but they say only one API key is in use. They have a small fleet of app servers behind an egress proxy. Attaching initial notes.

ajay: Which 429 headers are they getting? X-RateLimit-? any TTL info?

maya: Quote from customer: "x-ratelimit-limit: 60000
 x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
 x-ratelimit-reset: 167" — but they also get short TTLs (30–120s) and it varies per request. They reported it correlates with deploys.

devin: Do we have the request attribution in logs (api_key vs org vs nat ip)? Could be falling back to IP-bucket when auth check is slow.

maya: I've pulled a snippet from proxy logs and the request has both header key=sk-prod-abc123 and X-Forwarded-For: 10.3.2.14 -> egress-nat (203.0.113.45). customer says sometimes calls come from ephemeral containers.

rachel: If authz lookup latency > 200ms we sometimes attribute to egress IP for fast-path enforcement. That's intended but can cause cross-app shadowing.

maya: Customer says they see 429s for unrelated API keys owned by the same org. They only have 1 key in prod though. Could be rotation happening?

ajay: Can you ask for a reproducible curl that hits the same NAT IP and include the full response headers? Also need trace-id from our edge logs for one 429.

maya: Sent request for curl + response headers + trace-id. Customer replied with this repro: 
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123' \
  -H 'X-Client-Id: acme-service-a' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers they pasted: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 60000
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 51
x-attribution: ip=203.0.113.45;bucket=egress-small;reason=fast-path
trace-id: 01FZQFY2...xyz
```

devin: That x-attribution is the new fast-path fallback. It means the auth call missed and we applied IP bucket enforcement. That matches rachel's note.

rachel: Root cause possibilities: slow auth cache TTL, auth service latency spike, or proxy added a new preflight that strips API key occasionally (rotation/corruption). Also burst from other apps on same NAT could exhaust the bucket.

ajay: Short mitigation options to propose to customer: 
- Move to dedicated egress (if on Dedicated/Private) to avoid shared NAT buckets.
- Add a short cache-warming step (preflight token check) to reduce first-hit auth misses.
- Request we pin their API key to a higher per-key quota (temporary uplift).

maya: They asked for a quick repro we can run from our side. I forwarded the trace-id to devin and asked infra to replay that IP+headers.

quota-bot: [automated] Org acme-inc current aggregated IP-bucket usage: 59,842 / 60,000 (expires in ~50s). Observed 18 different source ports.

devin: I pulled the edge logs for trace-id 01FZQFY2...xyz — auth latency for that request was 312ms and auth service returned 200 but late. Edge applied fallback attribution to ip=203.0.113.45. Also saw ~120 requests in the preceding minute from same NAT IP tied to other org keys.

rachel: Action items: 
- Support: ask customer for rollout/deploy timing & if they run multiple services behind same NAT.
- Platform: add metric alert for auth latency >250ms causing >5% fallback at edge.
- SRE: consider increasing fallback threshold or using short token-caching on edge to reduce fallback rate.

maya: Customer confirmed they do short-lived canary containers that hit the API when restarting — explains bursts. They've requested a temporary per-key quota bump while they shift egress to a static IP pool.

ajay: I'll approve a short quota uplift to 90k for 24h while they migrate. Also I'll file a ticket to make the fallback attribution explicit in the docs.

devin: For internal followup I'll attach the sample logs and a small test harness that simulates 200 concurrent short-lived connections from same NAT to reproduce. (Will paste later.)

maya: Thanks all — I've communicated the uplift and suggested mitigations. Customer is verifying migration plan. :thumbsup:
